history.period: Conversion ceremony 14 October 1956; stupa constructed July 1978 - 2001; inaugurated 18 December 2001
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE: The CSV gives only 'Buddha Vihar, Nagpur' with no further detail, and Nagpur has dozens of local Buddha Vihars. This entry is researched as Deekshabhoomi, by far the most prominent Buddhist site in Nagpur and the one typically listed under the generic name 'Buddha Vihar' in temple/heritage lists; this identification should be confirmed by the dataset owner. NON-HINDU SITE: Deekshabhoomi is a Buddhist stupa and monument, not a Hindu temple. It is the sacred site where Dr. B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism with about 600,000 followers on 14 October 1956 (Ashoka Vijayadashami), administered by the Burmese monk Mahasthavir U Chandramani, taking the Three Jewels, Five Precepts and Ambedkar's 22 vows. Ambedkar chose Nagpur as the homeland of the 'Nag' people, early followers of the Buddha. After his death on 6 December 1956, the Deekshabhoomi Smarak Samiti built the present stupa (designed by architect Sheo Dan Mal, construction 1978-2001, inaugurated by President K.R. Narayanan on 18 December 2001) as a replica of the Sanchi Stupa - the largest hollow stupa in the world, with a 120-foot dome, four ornate marble gates depicting the Four Noble Truths, an inner hall with a sandalwood Buddha statue, a bronze Buddha statue, a marble column inscribed with the 22 vows, and a Bodhi tree (verify whether grown from Anuradhapura or Bodh Gaya saplings - sources differ). The site is regarded as a pilgrimage centre of Buddhism in India, drawing millions of visitors annually.

name: Buddha Vihar (Deekshabhoomi)
town_description: Nagpur, in eastern Maharashtra, is the state's winter capital and is known as the 'Orange City' for its citrus trade; it is traditionally regarded as the geographical centre of India (Zero Mile). A major commercial, educational and transport hub of central India with a Maratha-era heritage, Nagpur is globally recognised above all for Deekshabhoomi, the site of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's 1956 conversion to Buddhism.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur (approx. 9 km per the India Cine Hub listing; one travel guide says approx. 5 km - verify). Taxis and app cabs available.
travel.railway: Nagpur Junction (approx. 4 km per the India Cine Hub listing; one travel guide says approx. 10 km - verify). Autos and taxis available; Bajaj Nagar bus stop is the nearest city-bus stop.
travel.road: On S Ambazari Road at Bajaj Nagar / North Ambazari Road, in the heart of Nagpur (PIN 440020). Easily reached by city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis from anywhere in the city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March, when central India's weather is coolest. Dhamma Chakra Pravartan Din (14 October) is the most spiritually significant time but draws lakhs of pilgrims and very heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily approx. 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM (verify - one travel listing says 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM). Entry is free; maintain respectful silence and decorum inside the stupa complex.
